StackType.rationale: PowerStackType.Counter. The sim has no StackType concept; Power.on_stack (powers.py:64-66) adds unconditionally, which is exactly what PowerCmd.ModifyAmount does (PowerCmd.cs:236 -- no StackType branch). Third-file citations, not hashed here.

ShouldScaleInMultiplayer.rationale: Multiplayer-only scaling (MultiplayerScalingModel). Out of scope everywhere; the sim is single-player.

ModifyDamageMultiplicative.rationale: Constant checked: FlutterPower.cs:24 declares `new DynamicVar("DamageDecrease", 50m)` and :36 returns it / 100m, i.e. 0.5 -- powers.py:2206. Dyadic, so outside hook_dispatch G9. `target != base.Owner -> 1m` matches powers.py:2205-2207.

AfterDamageReceived.issue: The hook SLOT and the guards are right -- FlutterPower.cs:39 is AfterDamageReceived, cmds.py:121-122 is the sim's after-damage slot with the same CreatureBlow guard, and powers.py:2218 reproduces all three C# conditions (`target == base.Owner && result.UnblockedDamage != 0 && props.IsPoweredAttack()`), this one correctly reading `props` through valueprops.is_powered_attack rather than the card. THE GAP IS THE RNG STREAM of the stun's move re-roll. C# takes the next state from the last logged state on the MonsterAi stream: `base.Owner.Monster.MoveStateMachine.StateLog.Last().GetNextState(base.Owner, base.Owner.Monster.RunRng.MonsterAi)` (FlutterPower.cs:47). The sim calls `machine.roll_move(self.owner, self.owner._rng)` (powers.py:2233-2235) -- `_rng`, the monster's construction rng, NOT `_move_rng`. Every other move roll in the sim goes through MachineMonster._move_rng (monsters/state_machine.py:306-312), which is `self._hooks.combat.combat_rng.monster_ai` and whose own comment says move selection "happens on the MonsterAi stream (mirrors MonsterModel.RollMove(targets) => MoveStateMachine.RollMove(..., RunRng.MonsterAi))" and that `self._rng` "is untouched". EXECUTED on a parity combat seeded 933T39V18D with THIEVING_HOPPER_WEAK: `combat_rng.is_parity` True, `hopper._rng` is a plain `random.Random` and `hopper._move_rng` is a `GameRandomAdapter`, and `_rng is _move_rng` is False -- so the roll draws from the wrong stream and, worse, does not advance MonsterAi at all. This is the same defect class as power/aggression's (wrong RNG stream), and it is LIVE: the Thieving Hopper is ported Hive content, it self-applies Flutter (monsters/hive/thieving_hopper.py:113-114), and exhausting those stacks with powered attacks is the ordinary way to fight it, so any conformance replay that stuns a hopper diverges on the move chosen AND on every later MonsterAi draw. Secondary: `roll_move` MUTATES the machine's current state where C#'s `StateLog.Last().GetNextState(...)` queries the last LOGGED state, which are not the same state once a ConditionalBranchState is involved. Third-file citations, not hashed here.
